stories.title: Drever Partners Launches Pre-Leasing at Missouri Hotel-to-Residential Conversion Property
stories.excerpt: Drever Partners announced the start of pre-leasing for Live Oak Apartments, a new apartment community offering a mix of studio and one-bedroom homes in the heart of Branson’s Theater District. Located at 3011 W. 76 Country Blvd., Live Oak Apartments transformed a former hotel into a residential community that expands Branson’s housing inventory while helping address the city’s long-term housing needs. The community features 142 apartment homes, including studios, larger townhome-style studios, and one-bedroom apartments. “Live Oak Apartments represents our commitment to identifying opportunities where thoughtful investment can revitalize existing properties, expand housing options, and support growing communities like Branson for years to come,” said Ryan Wall, Acquisitions & Asset Management with Drever Partners. The property is managed by Key Management. “Live Oak Apartments reflects our commitment to creating professionally managed communities that provide convenience, value, and a place residents are proud to call home,” said Lisa Hicks, Regional Property Manager of Key Management. Where the apartment industry connects. Meet the owners, investors, developers, lenders, brokers, and service providers driving today’s multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Build relationships, uncover opportunities, and stay ahead of what’s next. bullets: Drever Partners converts Branson hotel to 142-unit apartment community.
Pre-leasing launched for Live Oak Apartments in Theater District.
Mixed-income studios and one-bedrooms address Branson housing shortage.
stories.summary: Drever Partners has begun pre-leasing Live Oak Apartments, a 142-unit adaptive reuse project converting a former hotel in Branson, Missouri's Theater District. The community offers studios, larger studio townhomes, and one-bedroom units. The conversion directly addresses Branson's long-term housing shortage while revitalizing an underutilized asset.
stories.impact: Signals that secondary markets like Branson are experiencing rental demand sufficient to justify conversion economics; adaptive reuse becomes feasible when new supply pipeline is constrained and tourism/service employment drives persistent labor demand. Indicates capital is flowing to smaller metros where land costs are low and entry barriers via conversions are attractive relative to new construction.

stories.title: Quantum Real Estate Advisors Brokers Sale of Midwest Retail Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Quantum Real Estate Advisors, Inc. has brokered the sale of a five-property shopping center portfolio located throughout the Midwest. The properties are in Illinois, Ohio, and Wisconsin and consist of roughly 67,000 square feet. The portfolio featured a diverse tenant lineup, including local, regional, and national tenants. The purchaser is a global real estate investment manager focused on acquiring niche property types, including essential service retail. The seller is a private syndicator based on the East Coast. Dan Waszak, Executive Vice President and Brett Berlin, Senior Vice President, represented the seller in the transaction. “This portfolio stood out because of the embedded rent growth,” said Berlin. “With leases across several of these centers rolling in the next one to three years, the mark-to-market opportunities gave the buyer a clear runway to push net operating income and improve operations at the centers.” The post Quantum Real Estate Advisors Brokers Sale of Midwest Retail Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Midwest retail portfolio (Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin) sold with mark-to-market lease upside.
67,000 sq ft, diverse tenant mix, favorable lease roll timeline.
Essential service retail focused buyer acquired from East Coast syndicator.
stories.summary: Quantum Real Estate Advisors brokered the sale of a five-property shopping center portfolio (67,000 sq ft) across the Midwest. The buyer, a global manager focused on niche property types including essential retail, was attracted by embedded rent growth and lease renewals rolling within one to three years that provided clear NOI improvement runway.
stories.impact: Low multifamily relevance. However, signals that essential retail with lease upside is attracting institutional capital; this may indicate stronger retail fundamentals in Midwest corridors, which can support mixed-use development feasibility and anchor tenant confidence for multifamily projects with ground-floor retail components.

stories.title: Zoneomics Introduces AI Platform for Zoning and Built Environment
stories.excerpt: Zoneomics, a zoning data and intelligence company, has launched Bassett.ai, an AI operating system for zoning and the built environment. Designed for real estate developers, urban planners, architects, brokers, lenders and legal teams, among other professionals, Bassett.ai is reportedly the first publicly available intelligence product to optimize Zoneomics’ library of streamlined zoning data, which includes every U.S. municipality with a population of greater than 25,000. “Commercial real estate and land development still rely heavily on PDFs, fragmented municipal websites and manual research,” said Matthew Player, CEO and co-founder of Zoneomics, which is used by Cushman & Wakefield, Stanford University and Crexi, among others. “Bassett.ai transforms that complexity into intelligence that professionals and increasingly AI agents can use to make better decisions in seconds. With responsive and interactive tools to access easy-to-consume zoning information, cities can run more efficiently, development project analysis and completion timelines can accelerate, and planners can have a trusted assistant and operating system to guide their work.” Via Basset.ai, users can ask natural language questions such as “What can I build here?” or “What zoning constraints should I be aware of?” and receive detailed, citation-backed answers covering permitted uses, development standards, parking requirements, dimensional controls, neighborhood context and other critical zoning information within seconds, according to Zoneomics. The platform is named in honor of Edward Bassett, a Brooklyn-born attorney and politician who is considered the father of modern zoning. The post Zoneomics Introduces AI Platform for Zoning and Built Environment appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Zoneomics launches Bassett.ai, AI platform for zoning intelligence across U.S.
Covers every U.S. municipality with population >25,000.
Enables natural language queries on zoning, entitlements, build constraints.
stories.summary: Zoneomics introduced Bassett.ai, an AI operating system designed to streamline zoning research and development analysis. The platform covers all U.S. municipalities above 25,000 population and allows users to query feasibility and zoning constraints via natural language. Clients include Cushman & Wakefield, Stanford, and Crexi.
stories.impact: Materially accelerates entitlement and feasibility analysis for developers; reduces pre-development timeline and consultant costs, lowering soft costs and improving project velocity. For TCR, shortens the window to identify buildable parcels, stress-test zoning in target markets, and move from acquisition to entitlement with higher confidence—especially valuable in supply-constrained markets where time-to-shovel is competitive.

stories.title: Colliers Brokers $18M Sale of Newly Constructed Self-Storage
stories.excerpt: Colliers arranged the $18.4 million sale of Sunset Self-Storage, a newly constructed self-storage facility at 5514 152nd St. E. in Puyallup, Washington. Executive Vice President Jacob Becher and Vice President Nate Fliflet represented both the buyer, BVDSS Puyallup Owner LLC, and the seller, Mitchell RE Holdings LLC. “Strong institutional demand and a highly competitive bidding process drove pricing for this transaction,” said Becher. “The South Sound continues to be one of the Pacific Northwest’s most active self-storage investment markets.”Completed in 2025, the facility features climate-controlled units, multistory elevator access, modern security systems and a variety of storage options. Located within the Spanaway submarket, it provides direct access to State Route 512, State Route 167 and Interstate 5. “Sunset Self Storage represents a rare certificate of occupancy sale in a growing market,” added Fliflet. bullets: Self-storage facility, Puyallup Washington, sold for $18.4M in 2025.
New construction, institutional buyer, competitive bidding drove pricing.
South Sound market noted as Pacific Northwest's most active self-storage.
stories.summary: Colliers brokered the $18.4 million sale of Sunset Self-Storage, a newly constructed facility in Puyallup, Washington, completed in 2025. Strong institutional demand and competitive bidding drove valuation. The South Sound submarket is characterized as one of the Pacific Northwest's most active self-storage investment markets.
stories.impact: Low direct multifamily relevance. However, indicates strong capital flows to Pacific Northwest industrial/alternative real estate and suggests robust demand for storage in Puyallup growth corridor; signals broader economic activity and population migration to South Sound that may support multifamily demand in the same markets.

stories.title: Five New Retail Tenants to Debut at Washington Union Station
stories.excerpt: The Union Station Redevelopment Corporation (USRC) announced a new wave of food and beverage and retail tenants coming to Washington Union Station. Five newly signed tenants are expected to debut in the coming months, adding to the station’s mix of retail and amenities. This lineup of upcoming tenants includes Andy’s Pizza, Housebar, Capo Deli, Joe & The Juice, and Springbone Kitchen. The latest additions build on significant retail momentum at the station, where nine brands have launched within the past six months, following an additional 12 tenants that welcomed guests over the previous year and a half. In total, 21 new tenants have opened at Union Station over the past 24 months. “As investment in Washington Union Station continues to accelerate, it represents a rare retail opportunity – combining historic significance, unmatched transit-driven foot traffic and its position as the District’s only enclosed retail and dining destination set within a Beaux-Arts National Historic Landmark,” Divina Biron, vice president of retail leasing at JLL. bullets: Washington Union Station adds five F&B/retail tenants (Andy's Pizza, Joe & The Juice, others).
21 new tenants opened in past 24 months; nine in last six months.
Station positioned as District's only enclosed retail in historic landmark.
stories.summary: Union Station Redevelopment Corporation announced five new food and beverage and retail tenants debuting in the coming months. In total, 21 tenants have opened over the past 24 months, with nine launching in the most recent six months, reflecting accelerating retail momentum at the transit-anchored historic landmark.
stories.impact: Signals strengthening demand for transit-oriented mixed-use and retail in Washington DC. Robust retail leasing at Union Station—a pedestrian hub—may correlate with renewed office recovery and downtown residential demand; developers considering TOD multifamily projects near Union Station and along WMATA corridors should monitor this momentum as validation of walkable, transit-served neighborhoods.

stories.title: Brookfield Asset Management Raises Record $77B
stories.excerpt: Brookfield Asset Management raised a record $77 billion in the second quarter of 2026, bringing its assets under management to more than $1 trillion, the investment firm reported in an earnings call Wednesday. Year-to-date, the investor has brought in $98 billion, more than half of what Brookfield raised for all last year. It also deployed $21 billion this past quarter. Brookfield’s seventh flagship private equity fund raised $6.7 billion during the quarter, while its sixth flagship infrastructure fund brought in $9.3 billion, putting both on pace to become the largest funds of their respective vintages. The firm also secured $5 billion in commitments for its first AI Infrastructure Fund. In another AI-focused venture, Brookfield increased its financing framework with Bloom Energy for AI infrastructure power projects to $25 billion, up from the $5 billion commitment announced in October 2025. “We can source and entitle power land, develop and operate large-scale AI factories, deliver behind-the-meter and baseload power, provide contracted compute, and pursue partnerships with some of the major stakeholders, including semiconductor players and hyperscalers,” said Sikander Rashid, Brookfield’s global head of AI infrastructure. “Not many firms can bring all of that together.” On the real estate front, Brookfield also raised $4.3 billion across segment funds and deployed $5.2 billion, buying a privately held U.S. manufactured-home portfolio and the taking private of an outdoor industrial storage portfolio. Brookfield also completed its purchase of Oaktree, buying the remaining 26 percent stake for about $3 billion. The move is meant to bolster Brookfield’s credit business. “We really see the upside for that business is on the revenue front, the ability to include Oaktree into Brookfield’s broader distribution, product development, multi-asset programs with our largest partners,” said Brookfield CEO Connor Teskey, who assumed the position in February. bullets: Brookfield raised record $77B in Q2 2026; $98B year-to-date.
Assets under management exceed $1 trillion; deployed $21B last quarter.

stories.summary: Brookfield Asset Management raised a record $77 billion in Q2 2026, bringing AUM to over $1 trillion. Year-to-date capital raised totals $98 billion, with $21 billion deployed in the quarter. The firm is heavily focused on AI infrastructure, securing $5 billion in commitments for its first AI Infrastructure Fund and expanding Bloom Energy financing to $25 billion.
stories.impact: Massive capital availability for alternative assets and infrastructure may compress multifamily cap rates and increase competition for conventional apartment deals; however, Brookfield's focus on AI and power infrastructure suggests some capital is flowing away from residential. Developers should expect continued institutional buyer activity in stabilized multifamily but may face softer land and development financing as debt capital gravitates toward higher-yield, longer-duration AI/infrastructure projects.

stories.title: Return-to-Office Gained New Momentum in First Half of 2026: Report
stories.excerpt: U.S. office attendance is on the rise, but the return-to-office trend remains a tale of two cities. In the first half of 2026, office visits nationwide rose 6 percent year-over-year, and achieved the narrowest first-half gap from pre-pandemic levels thus far, data from foot-traffic tracker Placer.ai shows. The six-month period of foot traffic marked acceleration from the 1.9 percent annual uptick observed in the same period of 2025. Office attendance is far from a full and even recovery, however. U.S. office visits remain 31.2 percent below 2019 levels, according to Placer’s August office market report. While Miami and New York are making strides toward baseline visitation levels, Denver and Chicago still have a long way to go. The hybrid workweek also appears here to stay –– for now. The report’s survey of 11 major U.S. markets revealed that office attendance diverges widely across geographies. Cubicles and corner offices are filling up in Miami, where attendance in the first half of the year was 11.5 percent below that of 2019. First-half attendance in Denver, on the other hand, remained more than 40 percent below 2019 levels. The “most improved” award for the period of January through June goes to West Coast hubs Los Angeles and San Francisco, with annual visitation upticks of 13 percent and 10.9 percent, respectively. The pair of cities achieved the report’s largest year-over-year gains. Hybrid workweeks have made a lasting impact on U.S. corporate culture, but the model’s popularity is waning in some markets. The country’s highest shares of Friday office attendance belong to Miami and Dallas, where roughly one in seven weekday office visits fell on a Friday. In Chicago, however, Fridays account for less than one out of every 10 office visits. This is the same city where personalized video platform Cameo announced last year a $10,000 raise for every new and existing employee that returns to its Fulton Market office four days per week. stories.summary: Office foot traffic in the U.S. rose 6 percent year-over-year in H1 2026, accelerating from 1.9 percent growth in H1 2025, according to Placer.ai data. stories.impact: Uneven office recovery reshapes real estate investment geography and multifamily demand patterns. Strong return-to-office in Miami and NYC will support Class A/amenity-focused multifamily demand near central business districts; weak Denver and Chicago recovery suggests sustained demand for remote-friendly suburban and secondary market rentals. TCR should prioritize institutional-grade infill multifamily in Miami/NYC office corridors while considering value/workforce segments in secondary metros where office demand remains depressed but population migration continues.

stories.title: Krea USA Nabs $62M Construction Loan for Lauderhill, Fla., Rental
stories.excerpt: Krea USA nabbed a $61.8 million construction loan for a multifamily development in Lauderhill, Fla., property records show. The financing from Abanca Bank covers the 385-unit Le Parc at Lauderhill development, at 3831 Northwest 13th Street, just east of the Lauderhill Mall and North State Road 7. The 10-acre development will include three eight-story buildings, including a day care operated by a nonprofit and no other commercial space on the ground floor. Construction started in March and is expected to be completed next year. The project has undergone a few changes since first being pitched in 2020. It was originally envisioned as a workforce housing development, with Vivian Dimond’s Bayshore Capital Grove as a partner. Fast forward six years, the development will have no rental restrictions, and Krea USA bought out Bayshore Capital Grove’s stake, Akrisht Pandey, Krea USA’s director of real estate, told Commercial Observer. Still, a tax abatement amounting to $9.1 million over 10 years, which the City of Lauderhill approved in 2022, will remain, Pandey added. Rents are expected to range between 100 and 120 percent of the area’s median income. The developer will build a public road. Krea USA, led by founder and CEO Mauricio Girault, specializes in mixed-income multifamily residential properties. In January, the Miami-based firm proposed building an affordable homeownership condominium in Miami’s Overtown neighborhood on land owned by the city, the South Florida Business Journal reported. A representative for Bayshore Capital Grove did not respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Krea USA secured $61.8M construction loan from Abanca Bank for Lauderhill, FL.
Le Parc at Lauderhill: 385 units, 3 eight-story buildings, completion 2027.
Project removed workforce housing restrictions; $9.1M tax abatement secured.
stories.summary: Krea USA obtained a $61.8 million construction loan from Abanca Bank for Le Parc at Lauderhill, a 385-unit development in South Florida. Construction began in March 2026 and is expected to complete in 2027. Originally envisioned as workforce housing in 2020, the project evolved into unrestricted market-rate rentals; Krea USA bought out original partner Bayshore Capital Grove. A $9.1 million city tax abatement over 10 years remains in place.
stories.impact: Demonstrates active construction financing availability in South Florida multifamily despite elevated rates; indicates builder confidence in Lauderhill submarket fundamentals post-pandemic. Shift from workforce to market-rate reflects rental demand strength sufficient to justify removal of affordability restrictions—signals strong rents and investor appetite in South Florida. For TCR, validates South Florida as an active development market with lender support and suggests upside to rents if workforce restrictions are removed at maturity.

stories.title: In Largest U.S. Multifamily Sale Since 2024, BlackRock Pays $1.63B in SoCal
stories.excerpt: BlackRock has acquired more than 3,600 rental residential units in Southern California in one of the region’s largest commercial real estate deals in recent memory. It’s also the largest U.S. multifamily sale since June 2024. One of the investment vehicles run by the asset management titan put down $1.63 billion for Camden Property Trust’s 11-property portfolio. The portfolio is 96 percent occupied, with 3,620 apartment units in Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside and San Diego counties. JLL Capital Markets announced the deal Wednesday after it represented Houston-based Camden in the sale, and arranged $566.6 million in agency acquisition financing for the buyer. The financing covers seven of the properties and consists of a five-year, fixed-rate, interest-only loan structured to allow each asset to be sold or refinanced independently. JLL said the deal is one of the biggest apartment portfolio deals ever completed in Southern California, and that the assets represent roughly 16.5 percent of the region’s average annual multifamily transaction volume by unit count over the past five years. The portfolio includes the Camden, a 287-unit Hollywood development with nearly 39,000 square feet of retail anchored by an Equinox gym; the 380-unit Camden Crown Valley in Mission Viejo; the 469-unit Camden Landmark in Ontario, representing roughly 5 percent of that city’s institutional apartment inventory; and the 132-unit Camden Hillcrest in San Diego, where JLL said no multifamily property with more than 100 units has traded in the past decade. “The significant investor demand for these best-in-class assets in supply-constrained markets underscores the strength of Southern California fundamentals, leading to significant liquidity at scale,” Blake Rogers, senior managing director and multifamily platform leader at JLL, said in a statement. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BlackRock acquired Camden Property Trust's 11-property SoCal portfolio for $1.63B.
3,620 units across LA, Orange, Riverside, San Diego counties; 96% occupied.
Largest U.S. multifamily sale since June 2024; JLL arranged $566.6M financing.
stories.summary: BlackRock acquired Camden Property Trust's 11-property portfolio comprising 3,620 units across Southern California for $1.63 billion, the largest U.S. multifamily sale since June 2024. Portfolio occupancy stands at 96 percent across Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, and San Diego counties. JLL arranged $566.6 million in agency acquisition financing (five-year, fixed-rate, interest-only) structured to allow independent asset sales or refinancing.
stories.impact: Demonstrates sustained institutional capital appetite for stabilized multifamily in supply-constrained SoCal markets; $1.63B transaction signals strong asset pricing power and investor confidence in Los Angeles/Orange County rents. For TCR, validates Southern California as core institutional market; indicates tight fundamentals (96% occupancy) support premium pricing. However, mega-cap deals by BlackRock may intensify institutional competition for pipeline projects—emphasizes need to control land early and move fast through entitlements to win off-market deals before institutional buyers consolidate.

stories.title: Blue Owl Capital Provides $106M to Refi Lowell Hotel in New York City
stories.excerpt: A historic New York City hotel has received a new round of debt financing. Kensico Properties has secured $106 million to refinance the Lowell Hotel, a 17-story, 74-key luxury boutique hotel on Manhattan’s Upper East that the firm purchased and redeveloped in 1984, Commercial Observer can first report. Blue Owl Capital provided the senior loan, which will replace existing debt, while CBRE’s Matthew Klauer arranged the transaction on behalf of Kensico Properties. “The Lowell represents one of the most storied and irreplaceable luxury hospitality assets in the United States,” said Klauer. “The hotel’s unmatched reputation, superior market position, and experienced ownership group made this an exceptional lending opportunity.” Located at 28 East 63rd Street just off the corner of Madison Avenue and a few blocks from Central Park, The Lowell Hotel opened in 1927. The hotel features 74 guest rooms and suites, many of which include private terraces, and features notable bars like the Club Room and the Pembroke Room. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Blue Owl Capital provided $106M senior refinance for Lowell Hotel, Manhattan.
Historic luxury boutique, 74 keys, Upper East Side; purchased/redeveloped 1984.
Replaces existing debt; loan arranged by CBRE.
stories.summary: Kensico Properties secured $106 million in debt financing from Blue Owl Capital to refinance the Lowell Hotel, a historic 74-key luxury boutique property on Manhattan's Upper East Side. Blue Owl provided senior debt to replace existing obligations, with CBRE handling transaction arrangement.
stories.impact: Low direct multifamily relevance. However, signals continued strength in high-end hospitality financing and institutional capital flowing to premium Manhattan assets, which correlates with strong luxury residential demand in same submarkets (UES). Validates continued institutional focus on Manhattan real estate, supporting confidence in luxury/premium multifamily development in Manhattan and mirroring strength in Class A office/residential submarkets.
